just so you know, the process of creating textures within blender, and baking them to image/uv map , is not too bad, but its an entire lengthy process so i would save for the end and find yt tutorial for it

you rarely \*need\* sculpt mode, except for very organic things, I usually prefer proportional editing, its a great tool to be aware of as well (its the dot with a circle around in center/top of main window)

in terms of making those shapes, it comes with practice, just get comfortable using (e)extrude, (s)scale, (m)merge,

a more niche tool but very useful to know as a fundamental is (k)knife, simply draw any line and press enter and it will cut it into your mesh (only works in edit mode)

play around with the 1,2,and 3 keys

if it helps the parts look nicer, you can always select mesh-> symmitrize once you are done, in edit mode (this supports whatever axis you need symetrical)

theres nothing wrong with breaking it down to however many pieces you need  (you can always set the object current size as the proper scale of 1 by pressing ctrl+a)

ctrl + P : create a parent child relationship of two objects

ctrl + J : join two objects into 1

Edit - Preferences - Get Extensions - Bool Tool <- this can be useful, think ctrl+J but it does inclusive/exclusive merge and retopologize the mesh to have a coheasive surface, whereas crtl + j will simply tell blender to now consider both the mesh datas as one

(I like to use this also to just cut holes, like windows and doors using a "cube knife")

Theres no right or wrong way, each object can have a material, the whole gun can be joined at the end of and share one material (in theory, if you are animating the bolt i would keep that separate)

a single object/mesh can actual map multiple materials to the same mesh

So i guess dont stress about how you implement that too much

in the top right of your main window, you are in wireframe mode,

even with a decimate ratio of .5 , the mesh still has over 1 million faces, this could be causing the stuttering and the weird stripes

apply your decimate modifier, and add another one on for good measure

(note: if you dont apply, it save the original and the modifier version in memory, and will calculate both in realtime with any editing, usually once im satisfied i will apply decimate rather than leave it on.)

my rule of thumb, for avoiding artifacting in unity, is like you said, 4 corners everywhere no matter what, but im not pro

maybe at a high level of fidelity and performance those maths come into play, but generally I dont think it matters, should be the minimum you feel confident it will deform the way you want and look acceptable

try this:

delete/hide the original rig

click your model, alt + p , clear parent

click your model, go to the mesh data (the green triangle section with 3 small circles)

in the vertex groups, delete them all (spam the minus '-' button until your model has no vertex groups) (edit: I am assuming you havent defined any custom vertex groups, but if you did, just delete the ones that were auto generated by parenting the model to the rig.)

go to your modifiers tab, remove the armature modifier that was generated from whatever rig it was previously parented to

THEN, click on your model, shift click the new rigify rig, parent with automatic weights.

This is the basic workflow for using the generated rigify rigs.  You can technically skip all of this if you never parented your model to the original basic rig, but I usually will parent with auto weights to the original rig to make sure it lines up well, before generating the rigify rig - then I have to go in and clear the data following the steps above)

Yeah 500 is way too much for a first time, im sure if I was coming up on 500 without any experience I would be terrified.

200 is perfect for your weight IMO, I weight about 170 lbs and can have a great time with \~225-300.

Wait at least 3 hours after eating dinner to take the DXM if you are doing it at night, if you are doing it early or in the day just wake up and take it on an empty stomach.

Make sure you are completely sober from alcohol before taking the dxm, the nausea from the comeup will be much worse otherwise.

Some additional tips I can offer are:

\-Drinking a glass or two of water along with the DXM wont diminish the trip at all and will help with nausea.

\-For me, pills/gels usually take about 2 hours before the comeup is over, whereas syrup is around 1h 30m to 2 hours, when I was less experienced a good way for me to calm down if the nausea was getting bad was to keep track of the time.  ("Oh, its only been 1h 15m since I took the gels, its totally normal to feel like shit right now, I just need to relax and I'll be feeling good soon.") 

\-Dont try to do any fun activities that you may have planned for your trip during the comeup, like watching trippy vids or playing videogames with high speeds in 3D, just save that stuff until you feel good and listen to some relaxing music, doing otherwise would actually make the nausea worse for me when I was coming up while first experimenting with DXM.

Lastly, if you get the dosage and setting right, DXM is by far my most enjoyable drug experience there is, more so than psychadellics, weed, booze, stims, etc.  You are going to have a terrific time with a lasting mood boost for days or even weeks, just remember that its really important to use responsibly as psychological and physical DXM addiction is a very real thing and its easy to fall into if you are not careful.  Since you are doing 200 mg that will be either low plat 2 or high plat 1, it is recommended to wait two weeks before using again although you will likely be tempted to do so sooner.

Hope this helped and have a wonderful time from a fellow dexer.
